```{r}
#| include: false
set.seed(812)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
# censored Poisson example used in several figures (Section 3):
# m exact observations, ncen observations known only to satisfy y < 2
yobs <- c(3, 2, 4, 1, 3, 2, 5, 3); m <- length(yobs); ncen <- 12; n <- m + ncen
lobs <- function(l) sum(dpois(yobs, l, log = TRUE)) + ncen * log(ppois(1, l))
lcomp <- function(l, z) -n * l + log(l) * (sum(yobs) + sum(z)) - sum(lfactorial(yobs))
Qfun  <- function(l, lt) lcomp(l, rep(lt / (1 + lt), ncen))
lam <- seq(0.4, 3.2, length.out = 300)
```

# 1. Overview of EM

## Setup and Motivation

- Observed data $Y$; parameter $\theta$; likelihood $L(\theta) = P(Y\mid\theta)$
- In many models $P(Y\mid\theta)$ is an integral (or sum) over latent or missing data $Z$:
$$P(Y\mid\theta) = \int P(Y,Z\mid\theta)\,dZ$$


**Terminology**

| | Likelihood | Log-likelihood |
|---|-----|-------|
| Observed | $L_{\text{obs}}(\theta) = P(Y\mid\theta)$ | $\ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) = \log P(Y\mid\theta)$ |
| Complete | $L_{\text{comp}}(\theta) = P(Y,Z\mid\theta)$ | $\ell_{\text{comp}}(\theta;Y,Z) = \log P(Y,Z\mid\theta)$ |

## The EM Algorithm

Start from $\hat\theta^{(0)}$. For $t = 0,1,2,\ldots$:

**E-step**: replace $\ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta)$ by the expected complete log-likelihood
$$Q(\theta\mid\hat\theta^{(t)}) = E_{Z\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)}}\big[\ell_{\text{comp}}(\theta;Y,Z)\big]$$

**M-step**:
$$\hat\theta^{(t+1)} = \arg\max_\theta Q(\theta\mid\hat\theta^{(t)})$$

Iterate until $\hat\theta^{(t)}$ converges.

**Caution**: $Q$ is an average of $\ell_{\text{comp}}(\theta;Y,Z)$ over $P(Z\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)})$; it is **not** $\ell_{\text{comp}}\big(\theta;Y,E(Z\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)})\big)$.

## $Q$ as an Average of Complete Log-Likelihoods

Fix $\hat\theta^{(t)}$. Each draw $Z^{(s)}\sim P(Z\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)})$ gives one curve $\ell_{\text{comp}}(\theta;Y,Z^{(s)})$; $Q(\theta\mid\hat\theta^{(t)})$ is their expectation (illustrated with the censored Poisson example of Section 3, $\lambda^{(t)} = 1.5$):

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
lt <- 1.5; S <- 10
Z <- replicate(S, rbinom(ncen, 1, lt / (1 + lt)))            # draws of the censored y_i
curves <- sapply(1:S, function(s) sapply(lam, lcomp, z = Z[, s]))
Qexact <- sapply(lam, Qfun, lt = lt)
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
matplot(lam, curves, type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 1, col = "gray60", xlab = expression(theta),
        ylab = "log-likelihood", ylim = range(curves) + c(0, 2))
lines(lam, rowMeans(curves), lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
lines(lam, Qexact, lwd = 3, col = "black", lty = 2)
abline(v = lt, lty = 3)
legend("bottomright", bty = "n", lwd = c(1, 3, 3), lty = c(1, 1, 2), col = c("gray60", "firebrick", "black"),
       legend = c(expression(l[comp](theta*";"*Y*","*Z^(s)) ~ "for 10 draws"),
                  "average of the 10 curves",
                  expression(Q(theta*"|"*hat(theta)^(t)) ~ "(exact expectation)")))
```

## Cross-Entropy and Kullback-Leibler Distance {.smaller}

**Definition**: for densities $P(z)$ and $q(z)$ on the same space, the **cross-entropy** of $q$ relative to $P$ is
$$H(P,q) = -\int P(z)\log q(z)\,dz = -E_P\big[\log q(Z)\big],$$
so $H(P,P)$ is the entropy of $P$, and the Kullback-Leibler distance is
$$KL(P\|q) = \int P(z)\log\frac{P(z)}{q(z)}\,dz = E_P\!\left[\log\frac{P(Z)}{q(Z)}\right] = H(P,q) - H(P,P)$$

- KL measures how much $q$ diverges from $P$; it is not symmetric ($KL(P\|q)\ne KL(q\|P)$ in general).

## Gibbs' Inequality {.smaller}

**Theorem (Gibbs' inequality)**: $KL(P\|q) \ge 0$, with equality iff $P = q$ (a.e.)

**Proof.** Since $\log x \le x - 1$ (equality iff $x=1$),
$$
\begin{aligned}
KL(P\|q) &= -\int P(z)\log\frac{q(z)}{P(z)}\,dz \ \ge\ -\int P(z)\Big(\frac{q(z)}{P(z)}-1\Big)\,dz \\
&= -\int\big[q(z)-P(z)\big]\,dz = 0 \qquad\blacksquare
\end{aligned}
$$
**Remarks:**

- Equivalently $H(P,q)\ge H(P,P)$: the cross-entropy is smallest at $q=P$. This is what forces the $H$-term to behave as needed in the ascending-property proof (next slides), and what makes $F(\tilde P,\theta)$ a lower bound on $\ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta)$ later on

## Simulation Check: $-E_P[\log q(X)] > -E_P[\log P(X)]$

$KL(P\|q) = H(P,q) - H(P,P) = -E_P[\log q(X)] + E_P[\log P(X)] > 0$ whenever $q\ne P$: draw $x_1,\ldots,x_n\sim P$ and compare $-\log P(x_i)$ (blue) to $-\log q(x_i)$ (red) at the *same* sampled points; the observations are shown (jittered) along the $x$-axis.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
mu_p <- 0; sd_p <- 1; mu_q <- 1.2; sd_q <- 1.6; nsamp <- 40
x  <- rnorm(nsamp, mu_p, sd_p)                   # samples from P
nlp <- -dnorm(x, mu_p, sd_p, log = TRUE)         # -log P(x_i)
nlq <- -dnorm(x, mu_q, sd_q, log = TRUE)         # -log q(x_i)

curve(dnorm(x, mu_p, sd_p), -4, 6, lwd = 3, col = "steelblue", xlab = "x", ylab = "density",
      main = "P(x), q(x), and the samples")
curve(dnorm(x, mu_q, sd_q), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
points(x, runif(nsamp, 0.005, 0.03), pch = 19, col = "gray30", cex = 0.8)   # jittered observations
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 3, col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
       legend = c(expression(P(x)), expression(q(x))))

ord <- order(x)
yr  <- range(c(nlp, nlq)); gap <- diff(yr)
plot(x[ord], nlp[ord], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "x", ylab = "negative log-density at sample",
     ylim = c(yr[1] - 0.12 * gap, yr[2]),
     main = expression(-log~P(x[i])~vs.~-log~q(x[i])))
lines(x[ord], nlq[ord], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)
segments(x[ord], nlp[ord], x[ord], nlq[ord], col = "gray70")
abline(h = mean(nlp), col = "steelblue", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
abline(h = mean(nlq), col = "firebrick", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
points(x, yr[1] - 0.09 * gap + runif(nsamp, 0, 0.05 * gap), pch = 19, col = "gray30", cex = 0.8)
legend("top", bty = "n", lwd = 2, lty = c(1, 1, 2, 2), pch = c(19, 19, NA, NA),
       col = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "steelblue", "firebrick"),
       legend = c(expression(-log~P(x[i])), expression(-log~q(x[i])),
                  bquote(mean(-log~P(x[i])) == .(round(mean(nlp), 2))),
                  bquote(mean(-log~q(x[i])) == .(round(mean(nlq), 2)))))
```

- The red dashed line (average of $-\log q(x_i)$, an estimate of the cross-entropy $H(P,q)$) always sits above the blue one (average of $-\log P(x_i)$, an estimate of the entropy $H(P,P)$); their gap is the (Monte Carlo estimate of the) $KL(P\|q)$


## Key Identity

For every $z$, $\log P(Y\mid\theta) = \log P(Y,z\mid\theta) - \log P(z\mid Y,\theta)$. Averaging both sides over an *arbitrary* distribution $\tilde P$ of $Z$ gives, for any $\tilde P$,
$$
\ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) = \underbrace{\int \tilde P(z)\log P(Y,z\mid\theta)\,dz}_{\text{average complete log-likelihood}}
+ \underbrace{H\big(\tilde P,\,P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)\big)}_{\text{cross-entropy}} .
$$

This identity is used twice: for the ascending property of EM, and for the alternating-optimization view of EM.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.4
par(mar = c(3.5, 1, 1, 1))
th <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 300)
lo <- function(t) 3.2 - 0.045 * (t - 5.2)^2 + 0.5 * sin(t / 2.2)   # observed log-likelihood
av <- function(t) lo(t) - (1.4 - 0.45 * (t - 3))                    # an arbitrary average complete log-likelihood
plot(th, lo(th), type = "n", ylim = c(-1.5, 4.2), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
mtext(expression(theta), side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 1.3)
lines(th, lo(th), lwd = 3, col = "steelblue")
lines(th, av(th), lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
text(0, lo(0) + 0.9, expression(l[obs](theta)), col = "steelblue", adj = 0, cex = 1.3)
text(9.9, av(9.9) + 0.5, expression(integral(tilde(P)(z)*log*P(Y*","*z*"|"*theta)*dz)),
     col = "firebrick", adj = 1, cex = 1.1)
for (t0 in c(3, 7.5)) {
    arrows(t0, av(t0), t0, lo(t0), code = 3, length = 0.08, lwd = 2)
    text(if (t0 == 3) t0 - 0.15 else t0 + 0.15, (av(t0) + lo(t0)) / 2 - if (t0 == 3) 0.4 else 0, expression(H(tilde(P), P[Z](.*"|"*Y*","*theta))), adj = if (t0 == 3) 1 else 0, cex = 1.2)
    segments(t0, -1.5, t0, min(av(t0), lo(t0)), lty = 3, col = "gray50")
}
axis(1, at = c(3, 7.5), labels = c(expression(theta[1]), expression(theta[2])), tick = TRUE)
```

## Ascending Property of EM

**Theorem.** $\;\ell_{\text{obs}}(\hat\theta^{(t+1)}) \ \ge\ \ell_{\text{obs}}(\hat\theta^{(t)})$.

Plug $\tilde P = P(\cdot\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)})$ into the key identity:
$$\ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) = \underbrace{\int P(z\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)})\log P(Y,z\mid\theta)\,dz}_{Q(\theta\mid\hat\theta^{(t)})} + H\big(P(\cdot\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)}),\,P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)\big).$$

Intuition: the M-step makes $Q$ larger, and the cross-entropy is smallest at $\theta=\hat\theta^{(t)}$ (Gibbs' inequality), so it can only grow when $\theta$ moves — hence $\ell_{\text{obs}}$ is increased.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.9
par(mar = c(3.5, 1, 0.5, 1))
th <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 300)
t0 <- 3; t1 <- 6                                         # theta^(t), theta^(t+1)
Q  <- function(t) 2.6 - 0.07 * (t - t1)^2                # Q(theta | theta^(t)), maximised at theta^(t+1)
H  <- function(t) 0.8 + 0.04 * (t - t0)^2                # cross-entropy, smallest at theta^(t) (Gibbs)
lo <- function(t) Q(t) + H(t)                            # l_obs
plot(th, lo(th), type = "n", ylim = c(-0.5, 5), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
mtext(expression(theta), side = 1, line = 1.8, cex = 1.3)
lines(th, lo(th), lwd = 3, col = "steelblue")
lines(th, Q(th),  lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
text(9.9, lo(9.9) + 0.35, expression(l[obs](theta)), col = "steelblue", adj = 1, cex = 1.3)
text(9.9, Q(9.9) - 0.35, expression(Q(theta*"|"*hat(theta)^(t))), col = "firebrick", adj = 1, cex = 1.3)
segments(c(t0, t1), -0.5, c(t0, t1), c(lo(t0), lo(t1)), lty = 3, col = "gray50")
segments(0.1, c(Q(t0), lo(t0)), t1, c(Q(t0), lo(t0)), lty = 3, col = "gray50")
segments(0.1, c(Q(t1), lo(t1)), t1, c(Q(t1), lo(t1)), lty = 3, col = "gray50")
for (x in c(t0, t1)) arrows(x, Q(x), x, lo(x), code = 3, length = 0.07, lwd = 2)
text(t0 + 0.15, (Q(t0) + lo(t0)) / 2, "H", adj = 0, cex = 1.3)
text(t1 + 0.15, (Q(t1) + lo(t1)) / 2, "H (larger)", adj = 0, cex = 1.3)
arrows(0.3, Q(t0), 0.3, Q(t1), length = 0.07, lwd = 2, col = "firebrick")
text(0.45, (Q(t0) + Q(t1)) / 2, expression(Delta*Q >= 0), adj = 0, col = "firebrick", cex = 1.1)
arrows(0.3, lo(t0), 0.3, lo(t1), length = 0.07, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue")
text(0.45, (lo(t0) + lo(t1)) / 2, expression(Delta*l[obs] >= 0), adj = 0, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.2)
axis(1, at = c(0, 10), labels = FALSE, lwd.ticks = 0)                       # the theta axis
arrows(9.6, par("usr")[3], 10.1, par("usr")[3], length = 0.1, xpd = NA)
axis(1, at = c(1, t0, t1), labels = c(expression(hat(theta)^(t-1)), expression(hat(theta)^(t)), expression(hat(theta)^(t+1))), tick = TRUE)
mtext(expression(theta), side = 1, line = 1.8, at = 10.1, cex = 1.3)
```


## Proof: Comparing Two Successive Points {style="font-size: 30px"}

**Proof.** With $\tilde P = P(\cdot\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)})$ and $P_\theta = P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)$, so $\tilde P = P_{\hat\theta^{(t)}}$. Subtract the key identity at $\theta=\hat\theta^{(t)}$ from the same identity at $\theta=\hat\theta^{(t+1)}$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell_{\text{obs}}(\hat\theta^{(t+1)}) - \ell_{\text{obs}}(\hat\theta^{(t)})
&= \big[Q(\hat\theta^{(t+1)}\mid\hat\theta^{(t)}) - Q(\hat\theta^{(t)}\mid\hat\theta^{(t)})\big]
+ \big[H(\tilde P,P_{\hat\theta^{(t+1)}}) - H(\tilde P,\tilde P)\big] \\[2mm]
&= \underbrace{\big[Q(\hat\theta^{(t+1)}\mid\hat\theta^{(t)}) - Q(\hat\theta^{(t)}\mid\hat\theta^{(t)})\big]}_{\ge 0 \text{ by the M-step}}
+ \underbrace{KL\big(\tilde P\,\big\|\,P_{\hat\theta^{(t+1)}}\big)}_{\ge 0 \text{ by Gibbs' inequality}} \ \ge\ 0,
\end{aligned}
$$
where $H(\tilde P,P_{\hat\theta^{(t)}}) = H(\tilde P,\tilde P)$ because $\tilde P = P_{\hat\theta^{(t)}}$, and $H(P,q) - H(P,P) = KL(P\|q)$. $\blacksquare$

## The Function $F(\tilde P,\theta)$ {.smaller}

For any distribution $\tilde P$ of the hidden data $Z$, $F$ has two equivalent expressions:

$$F(\tilde P,\theta) \;=\; \underbrace{\int \tilde P(z)\log P(Y,z\mid\theta)\,dz}_{\text{average complete log-likelihood}} + \underbrace{H(\tilde P,\tilde P)}_{\text{entropy of }\tilde P}$$

$$F(\tilde P,\theta) \;=\; \ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) - KL\big(\tilde P\,\Vert{}\,P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)\big)$$

**Why they agree.** Rearrange the key identity $\ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) = \int \tilde P(z)\log P(Y,z\mid\theta)\,dz + H\big(\tilde P,P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)\big)$ by moving the cross-entropy to the left and adding $H(\tilde P,\tilde P)$ to both sides:
$$\begin{aligned}
\int \tilde P(z)\log P(Y,z\mid\theta)\,dz + H(\tilde P,\tilde P) &= \ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) - \Big[H\big(\tilde P,P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)\big) - H(\tilde P,\tilde P)\Big] \\
&= \ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) - KL\big(\tilde P\,\Vert{}\,P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)\big).
\end{aligned}$$

## EM as Alternating Optimization {.smaller}

Using $F(\tilde P,\theta) = \ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) - KL\big(\tilde P\,\Vert{}\,P(\cdot\mid Y,\theta)\big)$ with $KL\ge 0$, EM alternates two maximizations of $F$:

* **E-step** = maximize $F$ over $\tilde P$ with $\theta = \hat\theta^{(t)}$ fixed: $KL \ge 0$ with equality iff $\tilde P = P(\cdot\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)})$, so the E-step sets $\tilde P$ to the conditional distribution of $Z$
* **M-step** = maximize $F$ over $\theta$ with $\tilde P$ fixed: the second term of $F$ is free of $\theta$, so this is $\arg\max_\theta Q(\theta\mid\hat\theta^{(t)})$
* **Tight Bound** = at $\theta = \hat\theta^{(t)}$ (after the E-step), $KL=0$, meaning the lower bound exactly equals the observed log-likelihood: $F(\tilde P,\hat\theta^{(t)}) = \ell_{\text{obs}}(\hat\theta^{(t)})$

## E-step and M-step on the Lower Bounds

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
par(mar = c(3.5, 1, 0.5, 1))
th <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 300); t0 <- 3
lo <- function(t) 3.5 - 0.15 * (t - 6.5)^2                      # l_obs
B0 <- function(t) lo(t) - 0.2625 * (t - 1)^2              # F(P~_{t-1}, theta): touches l_obs at theta^(t-1), maximised at theta^(t)
B2 <- function(t) lo(t) - 0.6 - 0.2625 * (t - 1.9)^2                       # F(P~, theta) for another P~ close to P~_{t-1}: below l_obs everywhere, below F(P~_{t-1}) at theta^(t-1)
B1 <- function(t) lo(t) - 0.1 * (t - t0)^2                     # F(P~_t, theta): touches l_obs at theta^(t)
t1 <- optimize(B1, c(0, 10), maximum = TRUE)$maximum             # M-step
plot(th, lo(th), type = "n", ylim = c(-4, 6.6), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
lines(th, lo(th), lwd = 3, col = "steelblue")
lines(th, B0(th), lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "gray45")
lines(th, B2(th), lwd = 2, lty = 3, col = "purple")
lines(th, B1(th), lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
points(1, lo(1), pch = 19, col = "gray45", cex = 1.2)
text(0, 6.3, expression(F(tilde(P)[t], theta) == Q(theta*"|"*hat(theta)^(t)) + H(tilde(P)[t], tilde(P)[t])), col = "firebrick", adj = 0, cex = 1.2)
text(0, 5.4, expression(phantom(F(tilde(P)[t], theta)) == l[obs](theta) - KL(tilde(P)[t]*"||"*P(.*"|"*Y*","*theta))), col = "firebrick", adj = 0, cex = 1.2)
segments(c(t0, t1), -4, c(t0, t1), c(B0(t0), lo(t1)), lty = 3, col = "gray50")
arrows(t0, B0(t0), t0, lo(t0), length = 0.08, lwd = 3, col = "forestgreen")
for (d in list(c(-1, 0), c(1, 0), c(0, -1), c(0, 1), c(-1, -1), c(1, 1), c(-1, 1), c(1, -1)) )      # white halo behind the E-step label
    for (yy in c(1.15, 0.6)) text(3.9 + 0.07 * d[1], yy + 0.14 * d[2], if (yy > 1) expression(bold("E-step:")) else expression(tilde(P)[t]~"="~P(.*"|"*Y*","*hat(theta)^(t))), adj = 0, col = "white", cex = if (yy > 1) 1.1 else 1.0)
text(3.9, 1.15, expression(bold("E-step:")), adj = 0, col = "forestgreen", cex = 1.1)
text(3.9, 0.6, expression(tilde(P)[t]~"="~P(.*"|"*Y*","*hat(theta)^(t))), adj = 0, col = "forestgreen", cex = 1.0)
points(t0, lo(t0), pch = 19, col = "firebrick", cex = 1.3)
arrows(t0 + 0.1, B1(t0) + 0.04, t1, B1(t1), length = 0.08, lwd = 3, col = "darkorange")
text((t0 + t1) / 2 + 0.2, B1((t0 + t1) / 2) - 0.45, expression(bold("M-step")), col = "darkorange", adj = 0, cex = 1.1)
arrows(t1, B1(t1), t1, lo(t1), length = 0.06, lwd = 2, code = 3)
text(t1 + 0.15, (B1(t1) + lo(t1)) / 2 - 0.1, expression(l[obs]~"is even higher"), adj = 0, cex = 1.0)
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(3, 3, 2, 2), lty = c(1, 1, 2, 3), cex = 1.0, y.intersp = 1.3,
       col = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "gray45", "purple"),
       legend = c(expression(l[obs](theta)),
                  expression(F(tilde(P)[t], theta)),
                  expression(F(tilde(P)[t-1], theta)),
                  expression(F(tilde(P), theta)~"for another"~tilde(P))))
axis(1, at = c(0, 10), labels = FALSE, lwd.ticks = 0)                       # the theta axis
arrows(9.6, par("usr")[3], 10.1, par("usr")[3], length = 0.1, xpd = NA)
axis(1, at = c(1, t0, t1), labels = c(expression(hat(theta)^(t-1)), expression(hat(theta)^(t)), expression(hat(theta)^(t+1))), tick = TRUE)
mtext(expression(theta), side = 1, line = 1.8, at = 10.1, cex = 1.3)
```

# 2. Example 1: Two-Component Normal Mixture

## Model and Likelihoods

$$Z_i \sim \text{Bern}(p), \qquad Y_i\mid Z_i = 1 \sim N(\mu_1,1), \qquad Y_i\mid Z_i = 0 \sim N(\mu_0,1)$$

Observed: $y_1,\ldots,y_n$. Hidden: $z_1,\ldots,z_n$. Parameter $\theta = (\mu_0,\mu_1,p)$.

**Complete likelihood**
$$P(y,z\mid\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^n P(y_i\mid z_i,\theta)\,P(z_i\mid\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^n \varphi(y_i\mid\mu_{z_i},1)\,p^{z_i}(1-p)^{1-z_i}$$

**Observed likelihood** (sum out each $z_i$)
$$P(y\mid\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^n\Big[\varphi(y_i\mid\mu_1,1)\,p + \varphi(y_i\mid\mu_0,1)(1-p)\Big]$$

## Model and Likelihoods (Continued)

The observed likelihood is a product of **mixture densities**, each the sum of two weighted normal components:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1)); mu0 <- 0; mu1 <- 4; p <- 0.3
curve((1 - p) * dnorm(x, mu0), -3.5, 7.5, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue", ylab = "density", xlab = "y",
      ylim = c(0, 0.3))
curve(p * dnorm(x, mu1), add = TRUE, lwd = 2, col = "firebrick")
curve((1 - p) * dnorm(x, mu0) + p * dnorm(x, mu1), add = TRUE, lwd = 3)
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(2, 2, 3), col = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "black"),
       legend = c(expression((1-p)*phi(y*"|"*mu[0])), expression(p*phi(y*"|"*mu[1])),
                  expression(f(y*"|"*theta) == "sum")))
```

## The Mixture Density

The marginal density $f(y\mid\mu_0,\mu_1,p)$ can be bimodal or unimodal depending on $p$ and $|\mu_1-\mu_0|$:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.4
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
mix <- function(x, mu0, mu1, p) (1 - p) * dnorm(x, mu0) + p * dnorm(x, mu1)
for (s in list(c(0, 4, 0.5), c(0, 4, 0.15), c(0, 1.5, 0.5))) {
  curve(mix(x, s[1], s[2], s[3]), -4, 7, lwd = 3, xlab = "y", ylab = "density",
        main = bquote(mu[0] == .(s[1]) ~ "," ~ mu[1] == .(s[2]) ~ "," ~ p == .(s[3])))
  y <- ifelse(rbinom(200, 1, s[3]) == 1, rnorm(200, s[2]), rnorm(200, s[1]))
  rug(y, col = "gray40")
}
```

Maximizing $\prod_i f(y_i\mid\theta)$ directly is awkward because of the sum inside the product; EM works with the complete likelihood instead.

## Complete Log-Likelihood

With $\log\varphi(y\mid\mu,1) = -\tfrac12(y-\mu)^2 - \log\sqrt{2\pi}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell_{\text{comp}}(\theta;y,z)
&= \sum_{i=1}^n\Big[z_i\log p + (1-z_i)\log(1-p) - \tfrac12(y_i-\mu_{z_i})^2\Big] + C \\
&= \Big(\sum_{i=1}^n z_i\Big)\log\frac{p}{1-p} + n\log(1-p) \\
&\quad - \frac12\sum_{i=1}^n\Big[z_i(y_i-\mu_1)^2 + (1-z_i)(y_i-\mu_0)^2\Big] + C
\end{aligned}
$$

- Linear in each $z_i$, so the E-step only needs $E(Z_i\mid y_i,\hat\theta^{(t)})$
- Given $z$, the parameters separate: $p$ is a Bernoulli proportion, $\mu_1,\mu_0$ are group means

## E-Step: Soft Classification

Given $\hat\theta^{(t)} = (\hat\mu_0^{(t)},\hat\mu_1^{(t)},\hat p^{(t)})$, Bayes' rule gives
$$
\hat p_i^{(t)} \equiv P(Z_i=1\mid y_i,\hat\theta^{(t)})
= \frac{\varphi(y_i\mid\hat\mu_1^{(t)},1)\,\hat p^{(t)}}
       {\varphi(y_i\mid\hat\mu_0^{(t)},1)(1-\hat p^{(t)}) + \varphi(y_i\mid\hat\mu_1^{(t)},1)\,\hat p^{(t)}}
$$

Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q(\theta\mid\hat\theta^{(t)}) &= \Big(\sum_i \hat p_i^{(t)}\Big)\log\frac{p}{1-p} + n\log(1-p) \\
&\quad - \frac12\sum_i\Big[\hat p_i^{(t)}(y_i-\mu_1)^2 + (1-\hat p_i^{(t)})(y_i-\mu_0)^2\Big]
\end{aligned}
$$

## E-Step: Soft Classification (Continued)

Left: at each $y_i$, $\hat p_i^{(t)}$ is the red share of the total height. Right: $\hat p_i^{(t)}$ as a function of $y_i$.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1)); mu0 <- 0; mu1 <- 4; p <- 0.3
f0 <- function(x) (1 - p) * dnorm(x, mu0); f1 <- function(x) p * dnorm(x, mu1)
curve(f0, -3.5, 7.5, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue", ylab = "weighted density", xlab = "y", ylim = c(0, 0.3))
curve(f1, add = TRUE, lwd = 2, col = "firebrick")
yi <- c(-0.5, 1.8, 3.2)
for (y in yi) { segments(y, 0, y, f0(y), col = "steelblue", lwd = 4)
  segments(y, f0(y), y, f0(y) + f1(y), col = "firebrick", lwd = 4)
  text(y, f0(y) + f1(y), sprintf("%.2f", f1(y) / (f0(y) + f1(y))), pos = 3, cex = 0.9) }
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
       legend = c(expression((1-hat(p))*phi(y*"|"*hat(mu)[0])), expression(hat(p)*phi(y*"|"*hat(mu)[1]))))
curve(f1(x) / (f0(x) + f1(x)), -3.5, 7.5, lwd = 3, xlab = "y",
      ylab = expression(P(Z[i] == 1*"|"*y[i]*","*hat(theta)^(t))))
abline(h = c(0, 1), lty = 3); points(yi, f1(yi) / (f0(yi) + f1(yi)), pch = 19)
```

## M-Step: Weighted Proportions and Means {.smaller}

$Q$ separates into a term in $p$ and terms in $\mu_1$, $\mu_0$.

| Update | Stationary equation $\;\Longrightarrow\;$ solution |
|---|--------|
| $p$ | $\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial p} = \dfrac{\sum_i \hat p_i^{(t)}}{p(1-p)} - \dfrac{n}{1-p} = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; \hat p^{(t+1)} = \dfrac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \hat p_i^{(t)}$ |
| $\mu_1$ | $\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial \mu_1} = \sum_i \hat p_i^{(t)}(y_i-\mu_1) = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; \hat\mu_1^{(t+1)} = \dfrac{\sum_i \hat p_i^{(t)}\,y_i}{\sum_i \hat p_i^{(t)}}$ |
| $\mu_0$ (weights $1-\hat p_i^{(t)}$) | $\hat\mu_0^{(t+1)} = \dfrac{\sum_i (1-\hat p_i^{(t)})\,y_i}{\sum_i (1-\hat p_i^{(t)})}$ |

Return to the E-step with $\hat\theta^{(t+1)}$ and recompute $\hat p_i^{(t+1)}$.

**Interpretation**: the M-step is the complete-data MLE with each observation split between the two groups according to its soft classification.

# 3. Example 2: Censored Poisson Data

## Truncated Distributions in Brief

Let $X\sim f(x)$ and $Y = I(X>c)$. Then $Y\sim\text{Bern}\big(P(X>c)\big)$, and the conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y$ is $f$ restricted to one side of $c$ and renormalized:
$$f(x\mid Y=1) = \frac{f(x)\,I(x>c)}{\int_c^\infty f(t)\,dt}, \qquad
f(x\mid Y=0) = \frac{f(x)\,I(x\le c)}{\int_{-\infty}^c f(t)\,dt}$$

For discrete $X$ the integrals are sums. This is exactly the distribution the E-step needs when an observation is only known to lie on one side of $c$.

## Truncated Distributions in Brief (Continued)

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)); cc <- 1
curve(dnorm, -3.5, 3.5, lwd = 3, xlab = "x", ylab = "density", main = "f(x) with cut point c")
xs <- seq(cc, 3.5, length.out = 100)
polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(dnorm(xs), rep(0, 100)), col = adjustcolor("firebrick", 0.3), border = NA)
xs <- seq(-3.5, cc, length.out = 100)
polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(dnorm(xs), rep(0, 100)), col = adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.3), border = NA)
abline(v = cc, lty = 2); text(cc, 0.38, "c", pos = 4)
text(1.8, 0.05, "P(X > c)", col = "firebrick"); text(-1, 0.1, expression(P(X <= c)), col = "steelblue")
curve(dnorm(x) * (x > cc) / pnorm(cc, lower.tail = FALSE), -3.5, 3.5, lwd = 3, col = "firebrick",
      n = 1001, xlab = "x", ylab = "density", main = "conditional densities", ylim = c(0, 1.6))
curve(dnorm(x) * (x <= cc) / pnorm(cc), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "steelblue", n = 1001)
abline(v = cc, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", bty = "n", lwd = 3, col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
       legend = c("f(x | Y = 0)", "f(x | Y = 1)"))
```

## Censored Poisson: Data and Likelihoods

$y_i \overset{iid}{\sim}\text{Pois}(\lambda)$, $i=1,\ldots,n$. The first $m$ values are observed exactly; for $i>m$ we only know $y_i<2$, recorded as $x_i = I(y_i<2) = 1$.

**Observed data**: $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ and $x_{m+1}=\cdots=x_n=1$. **Missing**: $y_{m+1},\ldots,y_n$.

**Complete likelihood**
$$\prod_{i=1}^n f^{\text{Pois}}(y_i\mid\lambda)\cdot\prod_{i=m+1}^n I(y_i<2)$$

**Observed likelihood**
$$\prod_{i=1}^m f^{\text{Pois}}(y_i\mid\lambda)\cdot\prod_{i=m+1}^n P(y_i<2\mid\lambda),
\qquad P(y_i<2\mid\lambda) = e^{-\lambda}(1+\lambda)$$

The second factor makes the MLE nonlinear in $\lambda$; EM sidesteps it.

## E-Step

$$
\ell_{\text{comp}}(\lambda) = -n\lambda + (\log\lambda)\sum_{i=1}^m y_i
+ (\log\lambda)\underbrace{\sum_{i=m+1}^n y_i}_{\text{missing}} - \sum_{i=1}^n\log(y_i!)
$$

For $i>m$, $y_i\in\{0,1\}$, and the truncated Poisson given $\lambda^{(t)}$ is
$$P(y_i=0\mid x_i=1) = \frac{1}{1+\lambda^{(t)}}, \qquad P(y_i=1\mid x_i=1) = \frac{\lambda^{(t)}}{1+\lambda^{(t)}}$$

$$\hat y_i^{(t)} \equiv E(y_i\mid x_i=1,\lambda^{(t)}) = \frac{\lambda^{(t)}}{1+\lambda^{(t)}}$$

Since $y_i! = 1$ for $y_i\in\{0,1\}$, the $\log(y_i!)$ term is a known constant and no further expectation is needed.

## E-Step (Continued)

The conditional distribution of a censored $y_i$ is the Poisson pmf restricted to $\{0,1\}$ and renormalized:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.4
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)); lt <- 1.5; k <- 0:6
barplot(dpois(k, lt), names.arg = k, col = c("firebrick", "firebrick", rep("gray80", 5)),
        xlab = "y", ylab = "probability", main = bquote("Pois(" * lambda^(t) == .(lt) * ")"))
barplot(c(1, lt) / (1 + lt), names.arg = 0:1, col = "firebrick", xlab = "y", ylab = "probability",
        main = expression("truncated to {0, 1}: " * P(y[i]*"|"*x[i] == 1)))
```

## M-Step and the EM Update

$$Q(\lambda\mid\lambda^{(t)}) = -n\lambda + (\log\lambda)\Big[\sum_{i=1}^m y_i + (n-m)\,\hat y^{(t)}\Big] + C^{(t)}$$

$$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial\lambda} = -n + \frac{1}{\lambda}\Big[\sum_{i=1}^m y_i + (n-m)\hat y^{(t)}\Big] = 0$$

$$\Longrightarrow\quad \lambda^{(t+1)} = \frac{m\,\bar y_{1:m} + (n-m)\dfrac{\lambda^{(t)}}{1+\lambda^{(t)}}}{n}$$

- The update is the ordinary Poisson MLE (sample mean) with each censored value replaced by its conditional expectation
- This works here only because $\ell_{\text{comp}}$ is linear in the missing $y_i$; in general, EM is **not** "plug in $E(Z)$ and maximize"

# 4. More Complex Applications

## Model-Based Clustering

$$Z_i\sim\text{Categorical}(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_K), \qquad Y_i\mid Z_i=k\sim N_d(\mu_k,\Sigma_k)$$

Multivariate, $K$-component generalization of Example 1. E-step: soft cluster memberships $P(Z_i=k\mid y_i,\hat\theta^{(t)})$; M-step: weighted means, covariances, and proportions.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.6
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
ctr <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, 3), c(1, 5))
Sig <- list(diag(2) * 0.8, matrix(c(1, 0.7, 0.7, 1), 2), diag(c(1.2, 0.4)))
cols <- c("steelblue", "firebrick", "forestgreen"); ang <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)
plot(NA, xlim = c(-3, 7), ylim = c(-3, 8), xlab = expression(y[1]), ylab = expression(y[2]))
for (k in 1:3) { R <- chol(Sig[[k]])
  pts <- matrix(rnorm(120), 60) %*% R + rep(ctr[k, ], each = 60)
  points(pts, col = adjustcolor(cols[k], 0.6), pch = 19, cex = 0.8)
  ell <- (cbind(cos(ang), sin(ang)) * 2.1) %*% R + rep(ctr[k, ], each = 100)
  lines(ell, col = cols[k], lwd = 2); points(ctr[k, 1], ctr[k, 2], pch = 4, lwd = 3, col = cols[k]) }
```

## Hidden Markov Models

Hidden states $h_1\to h_2\to\cdots\to h_n$ form a Markov chain; each observation depends only on its own state:
$$P(y_{1:n}\mid h_{1:n},\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^n P(y_i\mid h_i,\theta)$$

E-step: the forward–backward algorithm computes $P(h_i\mid y_{1:n},\hat\theta^{(t)})$ and $P(h_i,h_{i+1}\mid y_{1:n},\hat\theta^{(t)})$ without enumerating all $K^n$ state sequences. M-step: weighted transition and emission estimates (Baum–Welch).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.4
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1)); N <- 120; P <- matrix(c(0.95, 0.05, 0.1, 0.9), 2, byrow = TRUE)
h <- integer(N); h[1] <- 1; for (i in 2:N) h[i] <- sample(1:2, 1, prob = P[h[i - 1], ])
y <- rnorm(N, mean = c(0, 3)[h])
plot(y, type = "n", xlab = "i", ylab = expression(y[i]))
r <- rle(h); e <- cumsum(r$lengths); s <- c(1, head(e, -1) + 1)
rect(s - 0.5, par("usr")[3], e + 0.5, par("usr")[4],
     col = adjustcolor(c("steelblue", "firebrick")[r$values], 0.15), border = NA)
lines(y, col = "gray30"); points(y, pch = 19, col = c("steelblue", "firebrick")[h], cex = 0.7)
legend("topright", bty = "n", pch = 19, col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
       legend = c(expression(h[i] == 1), expression(h[i] == 2)), horiz = TRUE)
```

## Factor Analysis and the Common Pattern

**Factor analysis**
$$y_i = \Gamma x_i + \varepsilon_i, \qquad x_i\sim N_q(0,I) \text{ hidden}, \quad \varepsilon_i\sim N_d(0,\Psi)$$
E-step: $x_i\mid y_i,\hat\theta^{(t)}$ is normal with closed-form mean and covariance. M-step: regression of $y$ on the expected factors.

**Common pattern across applications**

1. Introduce a hidden variable that makes the complete-data model tractable
2. E-step: compute the conditional distribution (or expected sufficient statistics) of the hidden data
3. M-step: complete-data MLE with the hidden data replaced by expected sufficient statistics

## Summary

- EM maximizes $\ell_{\text{obs}}$ by alternating between $Q(\theta\mid\hat\theta^{(t)}) = E_{Z\mid Y,\hat\theta^{(t)}}[\ell_{\text{comp}}]$ and its maximizer
- Every iteration weakly increases $\ell_{\text{obs}}$; equivalently, EM is coordinate ascent on
$$F(\tilde P,\theta) = \ell_{\text{obs}}(\theta) - KL\big(\tilde P\,\|\,P(Z\mid Y,\theta)\big)$$
- When $\ell_{\text{comp}}$ is linear in sufficient statistics of $Z$, the E-step reduces to computing their conditional expectations
- Convergence is linear (often slow) and only to a stationary point; run from several starting values
